sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 793.6 ± 140.1 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Gq signaling EC50 assay: ETBR-Cys-P1 and ETBR-Cys-P3 variants showed EC50 values of 1.4–2.4 nM, comparable to wild-type, indicating full preservation of receptor activation.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly names ETBR residues 1–26 as the signal peptide and states the tag is placed immediately behind it, making insert_after_residue = 26 the exact validated junction. Residue 26 is G and residue 27 is E, read directly from the numbered sequence. The site is 72 residues from TM1 (boundary at 99), well clear of any TM constraint. L2 and L3 confirm functional surface expression of the tagged receptor. Full-length human ETBR expressed in HEK293 cells with Cys-P1 or Cys-P3 coiled-coil peptide tags inserted immediately after the endogenous signal peptide (ETBR residues 1–26), placing the tag at the mature N-terminus (residue 27 onward). Surface display was confirmed by fluorescence microscopy using complementary fluorescent peptides (Atto488-P2 or Atto565/TAMRA-P4) on non-permeabilized cells.

sources.claim: The sequences encoding the Cys‐P1‐ and Cys‐P3‐tag were positioned at the GPCR N‐terminus behind the endogenous signal peptides (SP) of the ET A R (ET A R 1−20 ) and the ET B R (ET B R 1−26 ).[ 30 , 31 , 32 ] The impact of the tag insertion on receptor activation was assessed in signal transduction assays using the G q signaling of both ET A R and ET B R.

Cell lines transiently expressing ET B (CHO-ET B ) were obtained using a mammalian HA-epitope tag expression vector, pHM6 (Roche Applied Science), which carries a cDNA encoding the recombinant human ET B receptor.

literature_notes: All five ledger lines (L1–L5) converge on a single physical junction: the mature N-terminus of ETBR immediately after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 26. L1–L3 (PMC9298254) provide a validated, functionally characterised site with Cys-P1/P3 coiled-coil tags; L4–L5 (PMC12015262) provide an independent surface-only confirmation with an HA tag whose exact insertion residue is not stated, so it is classified topology_derived. No ledger line mentions any internal extracellular loop insertion, any intracellular tag, or any insertion that abrogated function; therefore other_positions is empty. ECL1 (164–171), ECL2 (240–267), and ECL3 (346–362) are not supported by any ledger line and are not proposed.
